 1        III.   ACCOUNTING METHOD SUPPORTING THE BASE PERIOD

 2   Q.   What method of accounting does SPS use to record revenues and expenses

 3        associated with activities incurred as a result of business operations?

 4   A.   SPS uses the accrual method of accounting as required by GAAP and FERC USoA

 5        to record revenues and expenses. These revenues and expenses are recorded in

 6        accounts prescribed by the USoA and are recorded in accordance with the

 7        Commission’s rules.

 8   Q.   Have there been any revisions to accounting standards under the USoA since

 9        SPS’s last New Mexico Rate Case?

10   A.   Yes. Effective January 1, 2025, FERC revised the USoA for public utilities and

11        licensees by implementing Order No. 898. This revision was created to modernize

12        accounting methods for the changing utility environment by introducing new

13        functional classifications and accounts for renewable generation, energy storage,

14        and environmental credits as well as certain hardware, software, and

15        communication equipment.

16   Q.   How has SPS applied FERC Order No. 898 in this case?

17   A.   SPS has implemented all required changes and records all revenues and expenses

18        in compliance with Order No. 898. This requires SPS to reclassify certain O&M



                                              9
                                      Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                      Ross L. Baumgarten

 1        accounts and the expenses they contain. SPS witness Michele Kietzman discusses

 2        the impact of FERC Order No. 898 on capital accounts.

 3   Q.   Is the Base Period information provided in the RFP taken from SPS’s books

 4        and records?

 5   A.   Yes. The Base Period information submitted in this filing is taken from SPS’s books

 6        and records that are maintained according to the USoA. FERC prescribes the USoA

 7        for public utilities and licensees subject to the provisions of the Federal Power Act.

 8        FERC prescribes accounting classifications and guidance by which public utilities

 9        achieve uniform accounting records for use in financial reporting, ratemaking, and

10        other regulatory filings. These regulations are found and defined in the Code of

11        Federal Regulations 18 – Conservation of Power and Water Resources, Subchapter

12        C – Accounts, Federal Power Act, Part 101 – USoA. The Commission, in

13        17.3.510.10 NMAC, explicitly requires that SPS keep its books in accordance with

14        the USoA.

15   Q.   How did SPS determine the Base Period expenses included in the cost of

16        service and RFP schedules?

17   A.   Base Period amounts were taken from SPS’s General Ledger. As required by GAAP

18        and General Instruction No. 11 of the USoA, SPS employs the accrual method of



                                               10
                                      Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                      Ross L. Baumgarten

 1        accounting, under which SPS records an estimated amount for expenses incurred

 2        during the month. This may include amounts for which an invoice has not yet been

 3        received. After SPS receives the invoice or obtains more (or better) information

 4        related to an estimate, or there is a change in a regulatory or accounting principle,

 5        the expense is trued-up. In the case of an expense related to an invoice, the books

 6        are trued-up to the actual invoiced amount. This true-up typically occurs the

 7        following month. Thus, in a given month, expenses may include the accrual for the

 8        current month, the true-up of the prior month’s accrual to actual invoiced amounts,

 9        and adjustments as they become known.

10   Q.   Are there any other reasons the Base Period expense amounts shown on those

11        schedules may be trued-up?

12   A.   Yes. In general, true-up adjustments are also made necessary by such things as

13        resolved billing disputes, corrections of errors, changes in the method used to

14        develop estimates, the acquisition of more or better information about the cost

15        estimate, changes in regulatory principles, and changes in accounting principles.

16   Q.   How does SPS account for regulatory assets and liabilities?

17   A.   SPS accounts for certain income and expense items in accordance with ASC 980,

18        Regulated Operations. Under ASC 980, certain costs that would otherwise be

2   utility to recover those costs in future rates. In addition, certain credits that would

3   otherwise be reflected as income are deferred as regulatory liabilities based upon

4   the expectation that they will be refunded to customers in future rates.

5   Consequently, estimates for recovering deferred costs and refunding deferred

6   credits are based upon specific ratemaking decisions or precedents for each

7   particular item. Regulatory assets and liabilities are amortized consistently with the

8   period approved by the Commission.

 1             IV.     ACCOUNTING FOR ATTACHMENT Z2 TRANSACTIONS

 2   Q.      What do you discuss in this section of your testimony?

 3   A.      I provide background on the Attachment Z2 historical charges and the current status

 4           of related litigation, explain SPS’s accounting related to this issue and support its

 5           request to defer, as a regulatory asset or liability, the estimated New Mexico retail

 6           share of the final resettlement amount by Southwest Power Pool.

 7   Q.      Please describe Southwest Power Pool’s OATT Attachment Z2.

 8   A.      Attachment Z2 of the Southwest Power Pool OATT provides that transmission

 9           customers, generator interconnection customers, and entities that pay for a

10           Sponsored Upgrade 3 may receive revenue credits for network upgrades whose costs

11           have been directly assigned to them (“Creditable Upgrades”). 4 The revenue credits

12           provided to a customer that has been directly assigned network upgrade costs are

13           funded by and recoverable from transmission customers taking new transmission

14           service that could not have been provided “but for” the Creditable Upgrade, in the

15           form of credit payment obligations. Southwest Power Pool collects credit payment


              3
                The Southwest Power Pool OATT defines “Sponsored Upgrades” as “Network Upgrades,
     requested by a Transmission Customer or other entity, which do not meet the definition of any other
     category of Network Upgrades.”
            4
              The Southwest Power Pool OATT defines “Creditable Upgrades” as “Any Network Upgrade
     which meets the requirements of Section 1 of Attachment Z2.”

 2           customer or generator interconnection customer that was directly assigned the costs

 3           of the Creditable Upgrade is zero.

 1   Q.       What did the February 2019 Revised Waiver Order decide?

 2   A.       In the 2019 Revised Waiver Order, 7 the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

 3            (“FERC”) reversed its earlier July 2016 Waiver Order. The July 2016 Waiver order

 4            had allowed the Southwest Power Pool to issue retroactive Attachment Z2 invoices

 5            for transmission service from March 2008 through August 2016 (the “Historical

 6            Period”). The 2019 Revised Waiver Order held that Section I.7.1 of the Southwest

 7            Power Pool OATT, which includes a one-year limit on billing adjustments,

 8            Southwest Power Pool could not collect Attachment Z2 charges associated with

 9            transmission service rendered more than one year before the original billing date. 8

10            Because Southwest Power Pool first sought to bill customers for Attachment Z2

11            charges in September 2016, the ruling effectively established September 1, 2015,

12            as the cutoff date for recoverable charges.




              7 Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 166 FERC ¶ 61,160 (2019).
              8
                Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 166 FERC ¶ 61,160, at ¶ 47 (Feb. 28, 2019) (“[W]e find that section I.7.1
     applies to the transmission service charges in the [H]istorical [P]eriod invoices, notwithstanding the fact that
     Southwest Power Pool did not reflect the Attachment Z2 credit payment obligations in those invoices.”).

 1   Q.   Did the Revised Waiver Order require the Southwest Power Pool to refund

 2        any money?

 3   A.   No. Although the order withdrew the waiver that had permitted retroactive billing,

 4        FERC did not direct Southwest Power Pool to issue refunds immediately. Instead,

 5        it required Southwest Power Pool to file a report describing how it proposed to

 6        calculate and process any refunds owed under the decision.

 7   Q.   What has happened since FERC issued the Revised Waiver Order?

 8   A.   Southwest Power Pool has made several compliance filings explaining how they

 9        intend to refund the historical period resettlement given the complexity of

10        unwinding the Historical-Period settlements. On September 18, 2025, FERC issued

11        another order requiring Southwest Power Pool to submit additional details on its

12        proposed refund plan. The Southwest Power Pool filed the Compliance Filing with

13        the FERC on November 4, 2025, providing the additional details requested.

14        Additionally, the Southwest Power Pool requested the FERC issue an order

15        approving the refund plan and filed.

16   Q.   How do these rulings affect SPS’s Z2-related liability, if any?

17   A.   The Revised Waiver Order causes SPS’s liability for Historical-Period Z2 charges

18        to decline. This is because the Order disallows any credit payment obligations for



                                                 17
                                            Case No. 25-00___-UT
                                             Direct Testimony
                                                     of
                                            Ross L. Baumgarten

 1        transmission service occurring earlier than one year before Southwest Power Pool

 2        began billing for Attachment Z2 charges in 2016. Z2 charges for later periods could

 3        increase, however, because the recalculation of “creditable upgrades” depends on

 4        whether earlier amounts have already been recovered or reversed. Due to the

 5        complexity of the resettlement process, SPS is uncertain at this time what the net

 6        resettlement amount assigned to it will be. SPS will record the New Mexico retail

 7        portion of that net amount as a regulatory asset or liability, ensuring that any refund

 8        or remaining obligation is ultimately returned to or recovered from customers

 9        through future rate proceedings.

10   Q.   Has any court addressed the validity of the Historical Period charges?

11   A.   Yes. In Oklahoma Gas & Electric Co. v. FERC, the United States Court of Appeals,

12        District of Columbia (“D.C. Circuit”) affirmed FERC’s finding that the filed rate

13        doctrine barred the Southwest Power Pool from retroactively billing Historical

14        Period Z2 charges after the tariff’s one-year deadline, requiring Southwest Power

15        Pool to refund the charges. 9 Two years later, in Xcel Energy Services Inc. v. FERC, 10

16        the D.C. Circuit upheld FERC’s separate determination that Attachment Z2 was



          9
              11. F. 4th 821, 832 (D.C. Cir. Aug. 27, 2021).
          10
               77 F. 4th 1057, 1060 (D.C. Cir. Aug. 4, 2023).

 1        ambiguous as to the methodology for deciding when a transmission service request

2         triggered a Creditable Upgrade charge. Because the Southwest Power Pool’s refund

3         plan for the Historical Period is still pending at FERC, SPS continues to maintain

 4        the regulatory asset/liability to ensure that customers receive the correct

 5        jurisdictional share of the refunds or charges.

 6   Q.   How has SPS accounted for the estimated Attachment Z2 resettlement by

 7        Southwest Power Pool for the Historical Period?

 8   A.   Based on Southwest Power Pool’s calculated resettlement for the Historical Period

 9        as of December 31, 2024, SPS recorded a receivable and accrued an offsetting

10        regulatory liability of $13.6 million (total company). This figure is an estimate

11        because Southwest Power Pool’s final refund and resettlement process remains

12        pending before FERC and may change once FERC approves Southwest Power

13        Pool’s final compliance filing. Of the estimated resettlement amount, $2,431,707

14        has been assigned to the New Mexico retail jurisdiction, representing amounts

15        previously collected from customers.

 4               Power Pool OATT. Self Funding directly assigns cost recovery of the
 5               project to the customer requesting the upgrade.
 6
 7           •   FERC Account 456.1 revenues decreased by $1,084,830 as a result of

10               use transmission paths funded by SPS, credits are received as revenues.

15               calculated using SPS’s ATRR, which provides for cost recovery of SPS’s
16               transmission revenue requirement.
17
18           •   FERC Account 456.1 revenues increased by $13,586,127 as a result of
19               Schedule 11 revenues. The driver is changes in SPS’s ATRR for projects
20               eligible to be included and recovered through Schedule 11 of the SPP OATT.

21   Q.   How are Schedule 11 revenues and expenses related?

23        Power Pool which are aggregated to establish regional and zonal ATRR’s which are

24        then recovered from TC’s. A portion of the Schedule 11 expense allocated to SPS

25        and included in SPS’s Schedule 11 expense is for the recovery of SPS’s own ATRR.

26        The revenues received for Schedule 11 function as a partial offset to the expense

27        incurred for Schedule 11, driving the importance of including known adjustments

28        to both expense and revenue.
